hypotheses.title: Integrating White-Box Probes into the Boundary Assurance Stack for Autonomous LLM Agents
hypotheses.problem_statement: Current agent security frameworks like the Boundary Assurance Stack focus on external controls such as executable scope contracts and independent egress enforcement (arxiv:2610.12463v1), but lack internal cognitive monitoring mechanisms to detect unverbalized deception or hidden goals during multi-run coordination (arxiv:2610.12445v1).
hypotheses.proposed_solution: Combine the five-layer Boundary Assurance Stack with layer-and-token-aggregating white-box probes trained on the FIBS dataset to trigger automatic stop conditions when introspective deception is detected.
hypotheses.falsifiable_metric: Measured quantity: AUC of deception detection combined with Boundary Assurance Stack intervention. Comparison: Stack with probes vs Stack without probes. Result that refutes: Adding probes does not significantly increase the detection rate of unauthorized boundary breaches during simulated cyber tasks (p > 0.05).

supporting_findings.finding: automatic stop conditions, and evidence-based reauthorization
introducing a novel probe architecture which can aggregate information across many layers and tokens
